clients.name: St. Louis Sports Clinic
clients.sub: act_1074959853578156 · Paid Ad New Patient Pipeline

verdict.html: Last week landed 66 leads at $22.67 — the best week of the month, and part of a real turnaround: over the last 30 days spend is down 47% while cost per lead fell 33% and frequency dropped from a fatigued 3.4 to 2.7. The efficiency problem is fixed; the question now is whether to scale spend back up. Roster CPM rose 6% this week — this account’s gains are its own.

wins.b: Half the spend of the prior month, yet CPL $37→$25, CPM $19.66→$14.74, frequency 3.4→2.7. Same outcomes, far less money.
Opportunity score 100/100, zero anomalies, zero delivery blockers, every live ad in one consolidated ad set.

wins.t: The pipeline closes what ads send
wins.b: Matured cohort: 97 → 46 booked (47%) → 23 showed → 12 sold. Sold patients carry ~$1,686 each.
wins.s: GHL Paid Ad New Patient Pipeline

wins.b: GHL logged 233 opportunities vs Meta’s 236 leads for the same window — within 2%.
wins.s: GHL createdAt vs Meta · utmAdId join

problems.b: Video_67_v17.3.1 costs $5 more per lead ($28 vs $23) but sells at ~10% vs ~5% → $268 per sold vs $423. Meta’s CPL ranking hides this.
problems.fix: Shift a test slice of budget from v11.2.2 to v17.3.1 and judge on cost-per-sold. Small sold-n (6 vs 9) — run it as a 2-week test.

problems.t: Cheap in dollars, 60% above peer benchmark
problems.b: Meta puts the ad set’s cost-per-result 60% above comparable lead-gen advertisers — headroom peers are capturing.
problems.fix: With frequency back to 2.7, test an audience refresh / lookalike expansion, or check landing-page conversion vs peers.

problems.t: 11 paid leads stalling in early follow-up
problems.b: Eleven leads still open in New Leads / Manual Follow-Up 10+ days — ~$275 of paid leads idling before anyone books them.
problems.fix: Flag the list to the front desk for a same-day nudge. Raise in the weekly client check-in.

problems.t: 64% of spend on one ad, no cheap backup
problems.b: Video_67_v11.2.2 carries $3,804 of $6,428 (30d). Best performer, but both backups cost more per lead — a fatigue event would crater volume.
problems.fix: Keep 2–3 fresh challengers live at low budget so there’s always a proven next-in-line.

funnel.note: Real counts from the matured cohort (leads created wk of Jul 6). 12 sold × ~$1,686 ≈ $20k attributed. Last week’s 66 fresh leads aren’t here yet — they haven’t had time to book. At these rates they should land near 31 booked → 8 sold.

verdict.html: Scaling, and mostly working. Over 30 days spend rose 11% and pulled 14% more leads at a slightly lower CPL ($30.74), and last week set the reach and lead high (47 leads, 44.5k reach). The catch: 78% of spend rides on one ad, Video_Quote_v1.1.1, which Meta now flags as “below-average engagement — not spurring interest.” Still the cheapest lead source, but the only one at scale and showing fatigue signs. Line up a challenger before it tires.

wins.b: Over 30 days: spend +11%, leads +14%, CPL −2.4%, reach +7.6%. Last week set the reach and lead high — more budget is still buying more leads.
No delivery errors, no anomalies, opportunity score 79. And $38,800 of quotes are open in the Lead Pipeline right now (6 deals, $1.9k–$15k) — real money in flight.

problems.t: 78% of spend on one fatiguing ad
problems.b: Video_Quote_v1.1.1 is $4,238 of $5,809 and drove ~150 of ~186 leads — but Meta ranks its engagement Below Average (bottom 35%), “not spurring interest.” No proven backup runs at scale.
problems.fix: Build and launch 2–3 challengers now at low budget, so there’s a proven next-in-line before the workhorse craters.

problems.b: Last week spend +16% but CPL +8.6% and reach +27% — the extra budget bought reach faster than leads. A sign the audience may be starting to tap out.
problems.fix: Watch the marginal CPL as you scale; if it keeps climbing, widen or refresh the audience rather than just adding budget.

problems.b: One prospecting adset runs 47.5% above the CPR benchmark, and Meta’s top recommendation — connect the Conversions API — estimates −24% cost per quality lead.
problems.fix: Wire up CAPI to the Lead Pipeline you already run; it feeds Meta better conversion signal and directly targets the rising CPL.

funnel.note: GHL pipeline is wired (19 of 20 recent leads trace to Video_Quote_v1.1.1). The matured funnel and cost-per-sold populate on the live Monday run — this preview couldn’t page GHL history (a serialization hiccup that didn’t hit St. Louis).

verdict.html: This account is saturating a tiny audience. Reach was flat month-over-month (~12,700) while frequency climbed to 4.77 and CTR halved (3.05% → 1.46%). Cost per lead is $133 on just 16 leads, and the error feed shows broken pixel access on 9 ads plus a Page ad-restriction — a prime suspect for the collapsed lead tracking. Fix delivery and the audience before adding budget.

wins.t: CPL and CPM improved off a bad base
wins.b: Vs prior month, CPL $234→$133 (−43%) and CPM $48→$35 (−27%). Direction is right, even if the level is still high.
Meta returned no ranking/anomaly warnings and opportunity score reads 100 — the problems here are audience & setup, not creative quality.

problems.t: The audience is saturated — reach is maxed out
problems.b: Reach barely moved (12,709 → 12,722) while frequency jumped 3.4 → 4.77 and CTR halved to 1.46%. You’re showing the same ~12,700 people the same ads nearly 5×.
problems.fix: Expand the audience — new lookalikes, broader geo/interests, or a fresh prospecting audience. More budget on this audience just raises frequency.

problems.t: Delivery is broken on part of the account
problems.b: The error feed shows 9 ads without access to pixel 299…750 and a Page restricted from advertising. Broken conversion tracking is a prime suspect for the collapsed lead counts.
problems.fix: Fix pixel access (or rebuild those campaigns per Meta’s note) and resolve the Page restriction. Verify which are on live vs paused campaigns first.

problems.b: High cost, low volume. Lead tracking is unreliable given the pixel issue, so treat CPL as a ceiling, not a clean number.
problems.fix: Once pixel + audience are fixed, re-baseline. Don’t scale spend against a broken measurement setup.

problems.t: Heavy creative churn, only 1 ad live
problems.b: Nine of the top-10 ads by spend are already paused; only Video_TRT100_v5.1.1 is active (and spent $75). Lots of testing, nothing settled.
problems.fix: Lock in 2–3 stable creatives once delivery is fixed, rather than cycling variants weekly.

verdict.html: A small, expensive account. CPM is $94.74 — roughly 6× St. Louis — and rising ($77→$116 across the month), driving CPL to $165 on just 6 leads. Structurally it’s clean (score 97, no errors) and CTR is healthy at ~2.6%, so the problem is a tiny, costly audience, not the creative. Leawood is an affluent niche geo — either accept the premium or widen the net.

wins.b: CTR held ~2.6–2.9% (roughly 2× St. Louis) and frequency is healthy at ~1.8–3.0. People who see the ads respond — the creative works.
Opportunity score 97, no anomalies, no delivery errors. Only a minor A+ enhancements suggestion on the live static.

problems.b: $94.74 vs ~$15 at St. Louis, and it ran $77 → $78 → $116 → $111 across the four weeks on a tiny 3,483 reach. A small, expensive audience is the whole story.
problems.fix: Widen geo beyond Leawood or broaden the audience to bring CPM down — or explicitly accept the premium as the cost of a high-value niche. Decide deliberately.

problems.b: On 6 leads, so treat the exact number loosely — but the direction (up) tracks the CPM problem, not a conversion problem.
problems.fix: The CPM/audience lever above is the fix. Also worth pressure-testing the landing page for this niche.

problems.b: Video_HRT100_v1.1.2 booked the cheapest leads ($48.70, 3 leads) but is paused; the two live ads have no tracked leads yet.
problems.fix: Consider reactivating the proven winner instead of running unproven actives.

verdict.html: Steady, but slipping and mis-allocated. Over 30 days it’s fine — CPL $24 (−2.4%), CPM down 8%, reach up — but last week softened to 11 leads at $32, and CPL has crept up four weeks running ($19 → $32). The real issue is budget: Static_Quote_v1 eats 64% of spend at the worst CTR and CPL, while the cheap Carousel_Quote_v2 ($20 CPL, 2.77% CTR) is starved. Rebalance before adding spend. Low weekly volume — read single weeks loosely.

wins.b: On flat spend: CPM −7.6%, reach +7.9%, CPL −2.4%. You’re buying more, cheaper reach than last month.

wins.t: The carousel is the efficiency winner
wins.b: Carousel_Quote_v2 — 2.77% CTR and $20.04 CPL (best in the account) — on only ~21% of spend.

problems.t: 64% of budget on the weakest ad
problems.b: Static_Quote_v1 takes $950 (64%) at the lowest CTR (1.99%) and highest CPL ($26.39) of the delivering ads — dragging account CTR down 10.5% over 30d.
problems.fix: Shift budget toward the carousel and build carousel variants; cap or refresh v1. This is the single biggest lever here.

problems.t: CPL drifting up four weeks running
problems.b: Weekly CPL went $19 → $22 → $24 → $32. Even discounting the small-n weekly swing, the direction is consistent.
problems.fix: Watch next week; if the 30-day CPL crosses ~$25 sustained, rotate in fresh creative (the Reels 9:16 idea Meta suggests is low-lift).

problems.b: Opportunity score 80; Meta’s top recommendation is a CRM/Conversions-API connection estimated at −24% cost per quality lead.
problems.fix: Connect CAPI — it targets exactly the rising-CPL problem and is the highest-scored opportunity.

verdict.html: Small and getting pricier. Spend held flat month-over-month but leads fell 37% and CPL jumped ~60% to $103 — driven by a 23% impression drop and 29% CPM inflation, not conversion (CTR actually improved). Volume is low (7 leads/week), so read weekly numbers loosely. Two bright spots keep it out of the red: Meta scores it 98/100 with a prospecting audience running 235% below the CPR benchmark, and a freshly-launched creative is already driving CRM opportunities Meta’s attribution hasn’t caught up to.

wins.b: Opportunity score 98/100, no anomalies, no errors — and the prospecting adset runs 235% below peer CPR (results far cheaper than the industry cohort).

wins.t: New creative already working in the CRM
wins.b: vAI1.3.1 drove 4 of 5 recent pipeline opportunities even though Meta still reports its leads as “Not available” — attribution lags the real result. Don’t judge the fresh creatives on Meta’s lead column yet.

problems.b: Leads −37% ($64 → $103 CPL) on flat spend — from a 23% impression drop and 29% CPM rise (reach −19%). CTR actually improved, so this is delivery, not creative.
problems.fix: The audience/delivery narrowed — refresh or widen the audience to bring CPM back down. The lever is reach, not the ads.

problems.b: vU9.2.2 ($86 CPL) and vU11.2.1 ($92) — the cheapest leads — are off, while unproven fresh ads carry delivery.
problems.fix: Bring a proven winner back alongside the new tests instead of running only unproven creative.

problems.b: At 7 leads/week weekly swings are noise, and the account relaunched around Jul 20 (week 1 spent just $17), so the ramp distorts week-over-week too.
problems.fix: Hold the creative tests running; don’t react to single-week moves.

funnel.note: GHL pipeline is wired (fresh creative vAI1.3.1 is already driving opps here). Matured funnel + cost-per-sold populate on the live Monday run — this preview couldn’t page GHL history, and volume is low regardless.

clients.name: Posted Social
clients.sub: act_1252617339464304 · PostedSocial_PostedSocial_Leads_8/7/26 — leads campaign only (awareness campaigns excluded)

verdict.html: Just launched — first delivery Aug 10, so this is a 4-day read, not a verdict. So far: $448 spent, 5 leads at ~$90, testing two statics. Early CTR is healthy (2.18%) but CPM is high ($82) — expected for a cold B2B audience at launch. Too new to trend; next Monday is the first real week. Tracking only the leads campaign — the account’s awareness campaigns are excluded.

wins.b: CTR 2.18% in the first days — people are clicking. One creative, WebsiteGetsYouCustomers, is already at $73.86 CPL despite a $142 CPM.
Both active statics delivering, no errors, frequency low (1.8) — plenty of room to run before fatigue.

problems.b: Normal for a cold, narrow B2B audience at launch, but it’s what drives the ~$90 CPL. WebsiteGetsYouCustomers is running a $142 CPM.
problems.fix: Give it a week to clear the learning phase; if CPM stays above ~$80, widen the audience or test a broader interest set.

problems.b: 5 leads across 4 days. Any per-creative or CPL read is provisional right now.
problems.fix: Hold both statics running; make the first real call next Monday with a full week in hand.

clients.launchNote: This campaign first delivered Aug 10, 2026 — everything above is since-launch (Aug 10–13). The 4-week trend and week-over-week views need a couple of completed weeks and will build over the coming Mondays. First full-week read: next Monday.
